subject: How to Structure Varying Length Vector/DF Data

messages.author: 34d1b12964c01466
messages.subject: How to Structure Varying Length Vector/DF Data
parts:
My question is about how to structure/ tidy/ organize data.

Given a df users:

Users <- data.frame(Name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Cathy"), City = c("New York", "Dallas", "Los Angeles"))

In reality Users has many observations.

The Problem: I would like to add a 'route' for each user to get to, say, Chicago.  The route will be a series of lat/long, but will be of non-standard length: everyone's route will be different in number of steps.

I am using ggmap to do this, where

library(ggmap)
route(from = 'New York', to = 'Chicago', structure = 'route')

returns a data frame.

How should I properly store this data frame for each User observation?

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: How to Structure Varying Length Vector/DF Data
parts:
Well, the dplyr way is just to put the data frames inside the dataframe:

Users %>%
group_by(Name, City) %>%
do(
route = route(from = as.character(.$City),

) -> UserRoutes

I used to be very skeptical of this approach, but I've come around.

Best,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: How to Structure Varying Length Vector/DF Data
parts:
Well, I just think things are mentally easier to keep track of it you
only put vector-like things in your data frames. Once you start
putting complicated data structures inside your data frames it makes
things harder to reason about. The main alternative of repeating each
id variable as many times as there are legs in the route has it's own
pros and cons. As far as I've been able to tell you can't do it in
dplyr, but plyr is much more flexible;

detach(package:dplyr, unload=TRUE)
library(plyr)
UserRoutes <- ddply(Users,
"Name",
function(x) {
data.frame(City = x$City,
route(from = as.character(x$City),
